meta.safetyShort: Stop if symptoms worsen, radiate, or technique deteriorates. Follow physio guidance and read the full safety notes.
meta.safetyFull: Stop and arrange clinical assessment for new, changing, recurrent, or radiating symptoms before progressing loaded hinges, unilateral leg work, or plyometrics. Exercises should not cause symptoms that remain meaningfully worse the following day. Skill work, jumps, and loaded strength all stop before technique deteriorates. Seek emergency assessment for saddle numbness or bowel/bladder change. Seek urgent clinical assessment for new or progressive leg weakness.

workouts.warning: COMFORTABLE RANGE · NOT A FLEXIBILITY TEST
workouts.alt: Editorial illustration of an adult athlete performing cat-camel, a half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch, and a supported deep squat

cardSections.title: 1 · BREATHE + SPINE
cardSections.alternative: Small, comfortable cat-camel range

cardSections.title: 2 · HIPS + THORACIC
cardSections.alternative: Glute squeeze in the half-kneeling stretch

cardSections.title: 3 · ANKLES + SQUAT

workouts.intro: Perform this daily sequence gently as preparation. Keep the listed order and use a small, comfortable range.

detailSections.title: Complete sequence
items: Crocodile or 90/90 breathing — 5 slow breaths.
Cat-camel — 6 controlled repetitions in a small, comfortable range.
Half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch with glute squeeze — 30 seconds per side.
Open-book thoracic rotation — 5 repetitions per side.
Ankle rocks over toes — 8 repetitions per side.
Deep squat hold with supported breathing — 30–45 seconds.
Glute bridge — 8 controlled repetitions with a two-second hold.
Scapular wall slides or band pull-aparts — 8–12 repetitions.

detailSections.title: Back-sensitive morning
items: Replace only the deep squat and glute bridge with comfortable walking plus movements previously approved by the physiotherapist.
Retain the other comfortable mobility movements; stop or reduce range if symptoms worsen.

workouts.intro: Monday's formal strength session combines front-lever practice, upper-body strength, and moderate lower-body work. No plyometrics because Tuesday badminton follows.

detailSections.title: Preparation and skill — 12 minutes
items: Daily mobility shortened to 5 minutes.
Front lever block — 7 minutes.
Outdoor: scapular pull-ups 1 × 5–8; tuck front-lever hold 3 × 6–12 seconds with 45–60 seconds rest.
Indoor without a rated bar: hollow-body hold or dead-bug press 2 × 15–25 seconds; banded straight-arm pulldown from a rated anchor 2 × 8–12; optional seated band row 1 × 10–15.
Indoor prerequisite work is not equivalent front-lever exposure.

detailSections.title: Strength superset 1 — 3 rounds
items: Weighted backpack, ring, or deep-parallette push-up — 6–12 repetitions.
Strict pull-up or chin-up — 4–8 repetitions; indoor alternative: strong band row — 10–15 repetitions.
Rest 45–75 seconds after both exercises.

detailSections.title: Strength superset 2 — 2 rounds
items: Rear-foot-elevated split squat or reverse lunge — 6–10 repetitions per side.
Single-leg Romanian deadlift with kettlebell, dumbbell, or backpack — 6–10 repetitions per side.
Rest 45–75 seconds after both exercises.

detailSections.title: Trunk and accessory finisher
items: One or two rounds as time allows.
Side plank, initially without hip dips — 20–35 seconds per side.
Bent-knee calf raise with soleus emphasis — 10–15 repetitions per side.

workouts.cardSafety: If Tuesday + Wednesday include badminton, move B to Friday and omit C. Never place lower-body strength immediately before badminton. Stop if symptoms worsen, radiate, or technique deteriorates. Follow physio guidance and read the full safety notes.
workouts.intro: Use Thursday when recovered. If Tuesday and Wednesday both contain badminton, make Thursday mobility and easy skill work, move Full-body B to Friday, and omit Full-body C.

detailSections.title: Preparation, pistol practice, and eligible plyometrics
items: Daily mobility shortened to 5 minutes.
Pistol-squat practice — 7 minutes.
Thursday only, choose one: lateral bound and stick 2 × 4 per side; pogo hops 2 × 8–10; or on the following eligible session, split-step to random left/right cue 3 × 10 seconds.
Omit after Wednesday badminton and whenever badminton occurs later that day.
Do not perform Full-body B lower-body strength immediately before same-day badminton.

detailSections.title: Strength superset 1 — 3 rounds
items: Pike push-up, feet-elevated pike push-up, or wall handstand-push-up progression — 5–10 repetitions.
Ring row, cable row, one-arm kettlebell/dumbbell row, or heavy band row — 8–12 repetitions.
Rest 45–75 seconds after both exercises.

detailSections.title: Strength superset 2 — 2 rounds
items: Goblet squat with kettlebell/dumbbell or front-loaded backpack squat — 8–12 repetitions.
Weighted glute bridge, floor hip thrust, or hamstring walkout — 8–15 repetitions.
Rest 45–75 seconds after both exercises.

detailSections.title: Finisher and optional replacement
items: One or two rounds as time allows: Pallof press from a rated anchor or dead bug with full exhale — 5–8 per side; short-lever Copenhagen plank — 15–25 seconds per side.
In an eligible one-badminton week only, optional six-minute HIIT replaces—not follows—the finisher.
Use 30 seconds hard / 30 seconds easy with a back-comfortable mode; omit when sleep, back, knees, or badminton recovery is suboptimal.

workouts.intro: This third formal strength session is Saturday only when there is no weekend badminton. Sunday remains a recovery day before Monday Full-body A.

detailSections.title: Preparation and skill
items: Daily mobility shortened to 5 minutes.
Front-lever or weakest-skill practice — 7 minutes.
No mandatory jumps.

detailSections.title: Strength superset 1 — 3 rounds
items: Ring dip progression, parallel-bar dip, close-grip push-up, or weighted floor push-up — 5–10 repetitions.
Chin-up/pull-up, ring row, cable pulldown, or heavy band pulldown/row — 5–12 repetitions. Any band pulldown requires a rated anchor.
Rest 45–75 seconds after both exercises.

detailSections.title: Strength superset 2 — 2 rounds
items: Step-up on a verified stable surface or reverse lunge — 6–10 repetitions per side.
Kettlebell Romanian deadlift, kickstand RDL, or hamstring walkout — 8–12 repetitions.
Rest 45–75 seconds after both exercises.

detailSections.title: Finisher and optional replacement
items: Two rounds: bird dog with three-second reach — 5 per side; bear-plank shoulder tap or elevated shoulder tap — 6–10 per side.
In an eligible one-badminton week only, optional six-minute HIIT replaces the trunk finisher.
Use 30 seconds hard / 30 seconds easy with a back-comfortable mode; omit when sleep, back, knees, or badminton recovery is suboptimal.

cardSections.primary:
Tue · Handstand + V-sit
Wed · V-sit primary
cardSections.alternative: Fri · Front lever primary + handstand secondary

cardSections.title: 2 · HANDSTAND
cardSections.alternative: Then 3–6 quality kick-ups · Wrist prep first

cardSections.title: 3 · V-SIT PATH
cardSections.alternative: Optional leg extensions · 1–2 × 3–5/side

cardSections.title: 4 · QUALITY GATES
cardSections.primary:

workouts.intro: Skill-only mornings use 6–8 minutes of mobility, one primary skill for 7–10 minutes, and a secondary skill for 4–6 minutes only when time permits.

detailSections.title: Weekly sequence
items: Tuesday: handstand primary and V-sit secondary.
Wednesday: V-sit primary.
Friday: front lever primary and handstand secondary.

detailSections.title: Handstand practice
items: Wrist preparation: circles, palm pulses, and finger pulses for 60–90 seconds.
Chest-to-wall handstand — 2 × 20–40 seconds.
Wall toe-pulls or heel-pulls — 2 × 3–5 controlled attempts.
Freestanding kick-ups — 3–6 quality attempts, stopping before fatigue.
After 2 × 30 seconds chest-to-wall plus five controlled toe-pulls are clean for two sessions, shift more practice to kick-ups.
When three freestanding holds exceed five seconds in one session, progress to controlled entries and longer holds.
Regress to shorter wall holds if line, wrist comfort, or shoulder elevation deteriorates; use parallettes if wrists prefer neutral loading.

detailSections.title: V-sit pathway
items: Seated pike compression lifts — 2 × 6–10 repetitions.
Tuck L-sit or one-leg-extended L-sit on parallettes — 3 × 8–15 seconds.
Alternating leg extensions from tuck support — 1–2 × 3–5 per side when time permits.
After 3 × 15 seconds in tuck plus 2 × 10 clean compression lifts for two sessions, progress to one-leg extension.
Build a 3 × 10-second full L-sit before emphasizing hip elevation toward V-sit.
Regress when knees bend unintentionally, shoulders collapse, or back discomfort appears. Use a pain-free spinal and hip range; do not force compression through back pain.

workouts.intro: Monday provides formal lever practice and Friday is the primary skill morning; Saturday C can add an optional exposure. Actual lever work requires a stable rated bar.

detailSections.title: Outdoor or rated-bar option
items: Scapular pull-ups — 1 set of 5–8 repetitions.
Tuck front-lever hold — 3 sets of 6–12 seconds with 45–60 seconds rest.
When 3 × 12 seconds is clean for two sessions, use advanced tuck, one-leg extension, or slow tuck-lever rows.
The pull-up station must be stable and rated for body weight plus added load and dynamic use.

detailSections.title: Indoor or travel prerequisite work
items: Without a rated bar: hollow-body hold or dead-bug press — 2 × 15–25 seconds.
Banded straight-arm pulldown from a rated anchor — 2 × 8–12 repetitions.
Optional seated band row with deliberate scapular depression — 1 × 10–15 repetitions.
A stable, correctly rated indoor pull-up station materially improves consistency.

detailSections.title: Equivalence and safety
items: No-anchor rows and hollow work maintain prerequisites but are not equivalent front-lever exposure.
Never use an improvised door, furniture edge, or unstable anchor for high-tension pulling.
Stop before technique deteriorates; no grinding.

workouts.cardSafety: Stop if symptoms worsen, radiate, or technique deteriorates. Follow physio guidance and read the full safety notes.
workouts.intro: Practice on Thursday during Full-body B and on the weekend non-badminton morning. Select the easiest variation that preserves a stable foot, controlled knee path, and level pelvis.

detailSections.title: Practice sequence
items: Ankle and squat preparation — 1 minute.
Controlled full pistol, counterweighted pistol, or assisted pistol — 2–3 × 3–5 per side.
Use a three-second eccentric when full repetitions become inconsistent.

detailSections.title: Variation and progression
items: Select the easiest variation that preserves a stable foot, controlled knee path, and level pelvis.
Use only a verified stable support for assisted or box variations.
Add backpack loading only after 2 × 5 clean repetitions per side for two sessions.
Stop before technique deteriorates or symptoms worsen.

workouts.title: GREASE THE GROOVE
workouts.warning: KEEP AT LEAST 5 REPS IN RESERVE · NEVER CHASE FATIGUE

workouts.progression: GTG is the first training component removed when badminton performance, joints, legs, or back deteriorate.

workouts.intro: Use grease the groove on 2–4 days/week. Choose one primary movement per day and perform 2–4 mini-sets spread across the day.

detailSections.title: Rules
items: Keep at least five repetitions in reserve, or the equivalent margin for holds.
Do not use a movement within roughly 24 hours before or after hard training of the same pattern.
Mini-sets should stay fresh and technically clean rather than creating fatigue.

detailSections.title: Suggested starting doses
items: Pull-ups — 2 repetitions per mini-set when the bar is available.
Push-ups — 5–7 repetitions.
Handstand line hold — 15–25 seconds.
Band pull-aparts or scapular work — 8–12 repetitions.
Supported pistol pattern — 1–2 clean repetitions per side, no more than twice weekly, using stable support.

detailSections.title: Prohibited and removal rules
items: Do not use jumps, loaded pull-ups, ab-wheel repetitions, or fatiguing lower-body sets for grease the groove.
Remove GTG first when badminton performance, wrists, elbows, shoulders, legs, or back deteriorate.
